clue.text: Hater's need!

parts.note: surface reading: what someone full of hatred must have before they can stop hating
setter's reading: rearrange the organ of feeling and you get the word hater, so the hater literally needs that organ reshuffled

explanation.surface: A wry remark about what a hateful person really requires.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHANGE OF HEART would cure a hater, and changing the letters of HEART spells HATER, so the phrase works twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hates needs to soften their attitude, and a reversal of feeling is the idiom for exactly that.

clue.text: Comedian frames funny bit for singer

indicators.note: funny can mean odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
a frame goes round a picture, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a card is a joker, an amusing person
the three letters of bit, rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic sets up a funny routine for a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer' points the solver at a person; it is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The catbird is an American songbird known for its mewing call and mimicry, so it is a singer.

clue.text: Two naked males limiting insurrection

indicators.note: to limit is to bound on both sides, so one word is placed inside the other
naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters go and the inner ones remain

parts.note: males without its first and last letters
a coup is a sudden seizure of power

explanation.surface: A pair of nude men leading a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two naked males' reads as one picture, but 'Two' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple means a pair, so the phrase stands in for the number two.

clue.text: Gather leftover ends and nubbins, primarily!

definitions.text: Gather leftover ends and nubbins, primarily!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Instructions to collect scraps and stubs after a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, and its own first word is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To glean is to collect leftover grain after reapers, which is exactly picking up odds and ends.

clue.text: $5 found between circle and winding street: that's worth noticing

indicators.note: something winding twists about, so these letters are rearranged
found between places one piece in the middle with the others on each side

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
fin is American slang for a five-dollar bill
the letters of street, rearranged

explanation.surface: A five-dollar bill lying between a roundabout and a twisting road would catch your eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of interest deserves attention, so the phrase describes what merits a look.

clue.text: Yokel's fruit-flavored drink with potassium

parts.note: Hi-C is an American brand of fruit-flavored drink
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin's favorite fruit punch, fortified with potassium.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hick is an unsophisticated rural person, a plain synonym for yokel.

clue.text: Discombobulate brother with an offensive…

indicators.note: to discombobulate is to confuse or throw into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Confusing your sibling with a rude remark, continued in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which reads as a notion; here only 'offensive' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Abhorrent means repugnant or deeply objectionable, a strong synonym for offensive.

clue.text: …otion, however tolerable at first

definitions.note: read with the 'an' that closes the previous clue: 'an…otion' sounds as 'a notion'

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'it was cold, though'

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of tolerable

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: an offensive idea, though perhaps bearable.
explanation.walkthrough: The two clues run together as 'an offensive…otion'; the N has slid from 'a notion' to 'an otion', so 'otion' stands for notion.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is an idea or belief, and a thought is the same thing.

clue.text: One hundred boarding a ship to get high

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a passenger boarding a vessel goes inside it

parts.note: to ship goods is to send them
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A hundred passengers climbing aboard a vessel to get stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship' looks like a noun for the hundred to board, but it is the verb meaning dispatch.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to climb upward, so it means to rise or get high in the literal sense.

clue.text: Find start of trail and wander

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of trail
to rove is to wander

explanation.surface: A hiker locates the trailhead and sets off wandering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' looks like a verb but is the noun: a find, as in a treasure trove.
explanation.definitionFit: A trove is a valuable discovery or collection, which is what a lucky find is.

clue.text: Peruvian hollers for working together

parts.note: the Inca were the native people of ancient Peru
hoots are loud cries

explanation.surface: A Peruvian shouting encouragement at people collaborating.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in cahoots is an idiom for colluding or partnering secretly with someone.

clue.text: Solidarity for mischievous kids gives protection from punishment

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child; 'solidarity for imps' is imp unity
unity is solidarity

explanation.surface: Naughty children sticking together so none of them gets punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solidarity for mischievous kids' is read as imp unity, so the kids' word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is exemption from penalty or harmful consequences, a standard dictionary synonym.

clue.text: Accent a shoe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strong regional way of speaking, especially Irish
second meaning: a sturdy leather shoe with decorative perforations

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be an instruction to put an accent mark on a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names an Irish or Scottish lilt in speech and a perforated leather lace-up.

clue.text: Elegant bio, revised, is up for discussion

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A stylish biography, once rewritten, is open to debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A negotiable price or term is open to bargaining, so it is still subject to debate.

clue.text: Database constrains diminutive dork

indicators.note: to constrain is to hold in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: DB is the standard abbreviation for database
wee means tiny

explanation.surface: A computer system boxing in a little nerd.
explanation.definitionFit: Dweeb is American slang for a boring, socially awkward person, much the same as a dork.

clue.text: It involves a racket: running a foundation for illegitimate moneymaker

indicators.note: in a down entry a foundation sits at the bottom, so this piece goes last

parts.note: bad as in counterfeit or not genuine
a mint is where coins are made
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A criminal scheme: a front charity set up to launder a counterfeiter's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' suggests a criminal scam, but the definition means the stringed bat used in the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is played with a light stringed racket and a shuttlecock, so it is a game involving one.

clue.text: Staggered around erratically, etc., like Ronald Reagan

indicators.note: erratically means without regular order, so these letters are jumbled
around says one word goes about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: reeled means staggered
the abbreviation's letters, rearranged

explanation.surface: An unkind picture of an aging president tottering about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a jibe at Reagan's gait; the definition is simply that he won a second term in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Reagan won the presidency in 1980 and again in 1984, so he was voted back into office.

clue.text: Mentions singer having taken sedatives

indicators.note: something that has taken another thing holds it within itself

parts.note: an alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice
ludes is slang for Quaaludes, a sedative drug

explanation.surface: A news item about a vocalist found to have used downers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ludes is 1970s American slang for methaqualone pills, sold as Quaaludes.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude to something is to refer to it indirectly, a close synonym for mentions.

clue.text: Research lymphatic features in a clever way

indicators.note: to feature something is to contain it, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A study of the lymph system highlighting something smart.
explanation.definitionFit: Archly means in a sly, knowing, playfully clever manner.

clue.text: United Nations breaking boxes and bars

indicators.note: something breaking into another forces its way inside it

parts.note: loges are boxes in a theatre
UN is the abbreviation for United Nations

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers smashing up crates and barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' suggests prison bars or metal rods; here it means drinking places.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge is a comfortable bar room in a hotel or airport, so lounges are bars.

clue.text: Get to a point with a radio journalist, sometimes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to narrow gradually towards one end
second meaning: someone who records on tape, as a radio reporter may

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a coined noun: one who tapes, which a radio reporter does when recording interviews.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle or spire narrows to a tip; a person making recordings is one who tapes.

clue.text: Unpleasant person lying about sports-league game

indicators.note: one thing lying about another is stretched around it, enclosing it

parts.note: a pill is slang for a tiresome, disagreeable person
the NBA is the US National Basketball Association

explanation.surface: A nasty character fibbing about a professional match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like telling untruths; here it means lying around something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinball is an arcade game in which a ball is flipped around a sloping table.

clue.text: Likely to collapse from miserable, icy trek

indicators.note: miserable means in a wretched state, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A hiker on a frozen march so exhausted they might fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickety describes a structure so shaky and poorly built that it seems about to fall apart.

clue.text: Relative is held back by unfinished matter

indicators.note: a thing held by another sits inside its grip
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to count is to matter, as in every vote counts

indicators.note: back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member is delayed by business left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' looks like a noun but is the verb: to count, which loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is the child of an aunt or uncle, one kind of relation.

clue.text: That man's fear is originating in Mexico, perhaps

parts.note: that man's means belonging to him
panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: A man's dread is said to have come from south of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Hispanic describes people of Spanish-speaking heritage, and Mexico is one example, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Beginning to labor in long factory

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of labor

explanation.surface: The start of a shift at a sprawling industrial works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective for the factory, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works, so it can stand for a factory.

clue.text: Car's incomplete sound system

indicators.note: incomplete means the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: audio equipment is a sound system

explanation.surface: A complaint that a vehicle's stereo is only half installed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Audi is a German make of car, so the brand name is an example of one.

clue.text: White onion, maybe? That's an idea!

parts.note: light as in pale in colour
an onion is one example of a bulb

explanation.surface: Someone suggesting a white onion and being praised for the notion.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cartoon symbol: a glowing bulb over a head means a sudden idea.
explanation.definitionFit: In comics a lit lamp appearing above someone stands for inspiration, so the device symbolizes a bright idea.

clue.text: How cute sportsman in Oakland halfway kept up

indicators.note: halfway means only the first half of the word survives

parts.note: aw is the sound people make at something adorable
a player for the Oakland A's baseball team is an A
taken as written before being cut short

explanation.surface: Cooing over an Oakland player who stayed up only part of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept up' reads as one phrase, but 'kept' is wordplay and 'up' alone is the definition. The Oakland Athletics are known as the A's.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up in the morning means not asleep, so up here is a synonym for conscious.

clue.text: Transmitted germ of inspiration by telepathy and with feeling

parts.note: sent means transmitted

indicators.note: a germ is the seed something grows from, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of inspiration
telepathy works mind to mind, so done mentally

explanation.surface: A psychic beams a flash of inspiration to someone, with emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something sentimentally means doing it with tender emotion, so the adverb fits 'with feeling'.
